purpose: Conditions a report-only guard code must satisfy before an owner may enable it in memory_blocking_policy.json. Read by governance_tools.blocking_graduation_check.

rejected_criterion.name: consecutive_days_with_zero_findings
rejected_criterion.why_rejected: Zero findings is ambiguous between 'clean' and 'never ran, scope too narrow, matcher broken, or baseline swallowed it'. A quiet signal is evidence of nothing until execution coverage is proven separately.

_authority_note: An attestation must name someone in owner_registry, cite an authority document matching authority_ref_patterns, and carry the digest of this criteria file. These checks validate a declaration, not signer identity: repository JSON remains unevaluable until identity provenance is supplied outside the agent's write authority.

criteria.description: The guard is at census level 'invoked' or higher, so findings come from real runs.
The guard ran in a sufficient fraction of sessions closed inside the observation window.
No active (in-window) non-canonical writer violations remain. Historical debt stays advisory and is deliberately not counted here.
Known-positive and known-negative fixtures were both judged correctly, proving the check discriminates rather than always passing.
A sample of false positives and false negatives was reviewed and dispositioned.
A mutation run confirmed the check fails when the property it protects is broken.
A deliberately introduced in-window finding was observed actually blocking. Proving the check fires is not the same as proving the block lands.
The frozen baseline suppresses only historical debt and cannot suppress an in-window finding.
A documented break-glass path exists: the policy file carries an `enabled` switch, is writable, and states how to disable it.
The owner explicitly approved this enforcement profile. Never satisfiable by an AI agent.
